To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cigarette smoking causes a greater increase in pulmonary leukocyte recruitment in mice with functional C5 than in mice lacking C5, but does not induce a greater increase in chemotaxis of lung fluids in mice with functional vs mice without functional C5.
cigarette smoke exposure causes an increase in leukocyte recruitment to the lungs of C5-sufficient mice, and this increase in leukocyte numbers is partly mediated by C5 activation.
the fifth component of complement is necessary for maximal cigarette smoke induced pulmonary leukocytoses in mice, which is thought to be one mechanism by which cigarette smoking induces emphysema.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cigarette smoke on pulmonary leukocyte recruitment.
the mechanisms by which cigarette smoking causes an inflammatory response in the lungs of C57Bl/6J mice.
the role of C5 in the recruitment of leukocytes to the lungs of cigarette smokers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the C5 deficiency in C5- strains of mice is associated with an impaired response of the pulmonary alveolar compartment to cigarette smoke exposure, which is manifested as a decreased number of leukocytes recovered in lavage fluid.
the fifth component of complement, C5, is necessary for maximal leukocytosis to the lungs of cigarette smoke-exposed mice.
the presence of C5 in the lung is necessary for maximal cigarette smoke-induced pulmonary leukocytosisis in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cigarette smoke exposure causes a significant increase in pulmonary leukocyte recruitment in mice, and that this increase is partly mediated by C5.
C5 deficiency in mice attenuates pulmonary leukocyte recruitment in response to cigarette smoke.
C5 is required for the full expression of cigarette smoke-induced leukocyte influx and chemotaxis in the lungs of C5+ mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C5 is a critical component of the inflammatory response to smoke exposure.
the C5 component of complement is required for maximal pulmonary leukocyte recruitment in mice chronically challenged with cigarette smoke.
cigarette smoking induces pulmonary inflammation in mice by mechanisms that are partly dependent on the complement protein C5.
